A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRIM-KV research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, throughput measurements, ablations, and token-retention analyses in the main text and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and qualitative analyses and reports revised results across several benchmarks, including LongMemEval and LongBench-V2.

M1.justification: The specified training procedure changes materially. Equation (3) replaces exp(beta_i^(t-i) q_t^T k_i) with beta_i^(t-i) exp(q_t^T k_i), changing how retention affects attention. Equation (5) replaces uniform normalization by T(T-M) with per-step weighting by 1/t followed by averaging over T. The gate architecture and inference eviction algorithm remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether these revisions correct the implementation or its description.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluated tasks remain the same, including math reasoning, LongProc, LongMemEval, SCBench, LongBench, and LongBench-V2. Chunk-prefill evaluation on Phi3-mini-128K with LongAlpaca already appeared in v1 Appendix B.3; its addition to v2 Section 5.2 does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their baseline membership: SeerAttn-R, R-KV, SnapKV, H2O, StreamingLLM, KeyDiff, LocRet, and full-cache inference appear in the same relevant experiments. LocRet was already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.3, despite receiving greater main-text visibility in v2.

E3.justification: Reported training capacities change from 512 to 256 for long generation, 4096 to 1024 in Appendix B.2, and 2048 to 512 for chunk prefilling. The stated gate-bias initialization changes from 8 to 18. The LongMemEval evaluation grid also loses the 12,288-token budget. These are substantive reported setting revisions, not merely newly disclosed details; they do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix B.4's broader objective sweep, including reverse-KL comparisons in Figure 9, is removed, while the main objective-component table remains. Appendix C removes three token-retention-score visualizations and revises the selected heads shown in final-cache case studies. Dataset-transfer, gate-architecture, capacity-sensitivity, and overview matrix analyses remain, so the analytical program is largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report pass@1 averaged over 64 completion samples for AIME24 and eight for GSM8K/MATH-500. No new seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Results change across multiple benchmarks. LongMemEval accuracy at a 32,768-token evaluation budget changes from 48.2 to 44.8 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 8), while LongBench-V2 average accuracy changes from 30.68 to 34.09 (Tables 9 and 10). HTML-to-TSV at the 8192-token budget changes from 58.2 to 48.7 for the 0.5K task, losing its advantage over full-cache 49.0. Math and SCBench results also change, and the 12,288-token LongMemEval entries disappear. Changed training formulations and settings prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equations (1), (3), and (5) receive substantive mathematical revisions. In Equation (1), multiplying exp(q_t^T k_i) by the binary mask correctly gives evicted tokens zero weight; v1 instead placed the mask inside the exponential, leaving exp(0) weight. The revised retention definition also supports the newly stated additive-logit expression q_t^T k_i + (t-i) log(beta_i). These repair central definitions rather than merely change notation; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction revises the headline advantage over SeerAttn-R from 58.4% to 58.9% and explicitly describes it as a relative pass@1 gain. The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: learned intrinsic token importance, effective memory-bounded inference, occasional full-cache outperformance, and interpretability.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the LongMemEval interpretation from matching full-cache performance at 25% memory to maintaining good performance. It adds the additive-logit-bias explanation and removes the conjecture that smaller DeepSeek-Llama gains reflect lower attention sparsity. Removed appendix captions also eliminate specific interpretations about final-digit representations and instruction-following heads. The broader regularization, head-specialization, and applicability discussions remain.

D1.justification: The reported capacity and bias hyperparameters are revised, providing different reproduction settings. Other implementation information remains substantially unchanged: the 512-wide gate MLP, frozen backbone, learning rate, hardware, kernels, training-data descriptions, source-code address, and checkpoint-release statement. The throughput information highlighted in v2's main text already existed in v1 Appendix A.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds Press et al. (2021) when connecting retention gating to additive attention biases. It removes the RULER and InfiniteBench citations accompanying the shortened SCBench description. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against heuristic eviction, retrieval, and trainable forgetting methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the brain-inspired explanation and qualitative discussion, divides Section 5.2 into long-context decoding and chunk-prefilling discussions, and adds a corporate disclaimer. It also updates the publication header and first author's affiliation. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The supplementary visual presentation is substantially revised: the objective-sweep figure and three retention-score displays disappear, and ten final-cache token displays become seven revised examples. v2 also adds a main-text LongBench-V2 summary table and relocates several tables and figures. The overview retention and eviction matrices are retained and renumbered, not newly added.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equations (1) and (3) resolves an important flaw in the paper's central mathematical specification: zero retention previously left nonzero exponential weight, whereas v2's formulation actually suppresses or excludes tokens as intended. The more restrained LongMemEval interpretation also better matches the reported evidence. These substantial correctness gains outweigh the reduced supplementary analysis, although editing inconsistencies remain: Section 5.3 still promises the removed reverse-KL analysis, and Appendix B.3 retains a 6.5% LongBench-V2 gain despite Table 10 reporting 18.41%.
